name: Hair Physics Simulation
description: Validates hair movement against physics simulation models — AI-generated hair often violates gravity and inertia constraints.
mechanism:
This method detects AI-generated video by analyzing whether hair movement obeys the physical laws governing flexible strand dynamics — gravity, inertia, inter-strand friction, and aerodynamic drag:

1. **Hair Strand Tracking and Segmentation**: The method segments hair regions using a semantic segmentation network (BiSeNet) and tracks individual visible hair strand bundles across frames using optical flow constrained to the hair mask. Hair strands are parameterized as curves with control points tracked over time. The method identifies hair regions with sufficient contrast against background (e.g., strands against skin or clothing) for reliable tracking. Key measurements include: strand tip displacement, strand curvature changes, and relative motion between adjacent strand bundles.

2. **Gravitational Consistency Validation**: Real hair in motion always returns toward the gravitational resting position — strands exhibit underdamped oscillatory behavior described by the damped harmonic oscillator model with natural frequency depending on strand length and stiffness. When disturbed (by head movement, wind), real hair overshoots, oscillates with decreasing amplitude, and settles with time constant τ = 0.3–1.0 seconds (depending on hair length and type). The method tracks strand displacement relative to the gravitational rest position and validates this oscillatory decay. AI-generated hair often: (a) moves without returning to rest (persistent drift), (b) stops too suddenly (overdamped behavior inconsistent with hair stiffness), or (c) oscillates at physically incorrect frequencies.

3. **Inertial Response to Head Motion**: When the head changes direction, real hair exhibits inertial lag — hair continues moving in the previous direction for several frames before reversing, creating a characteristic S-curve in the strand trajectory. The lag magnitude depends on strand length, position on the head, and velocity change. The method estimates head motion from facial landmark tracking and predicts the expected hair inertial response. AI-generated hair typically moves synchronously with the head (no lag), moves with incorrect lag timing, or produces motion that violates conservation of angular momentum.

4. **Inter-Strand Coherence Analysis**: Real hair moves as a coherent mass — adjacent strands move similarly (high spatial correlation) with smooth variation across the hair volume. The inter-strand friction model means neighboring strands cannot have radically different velocities. The method measures the spatial correlation of strand-level optical flow across the hair region and computes the strain (velocity gradient) between adjacent strand bundles. Normal strain values are < 0.3 per frame for natural hair motion. AI-generated hair often produces high strain values (adjacent strands moving in different directions) or unnaturally uniform motion (zero strain, all strands moving identically as a rigid body).
parameters:
Hair segmentation: BiSeNet semantic parsing
Strand tracking: optical flow constrained to hair mask
Damped oscillator model: τ = 0.3–1.0 s (hair length dependent)
Inertial lag estimation: head velocity from facial landmarks
Spatial correlation analysis: 8-connected neighborhood flow comparison
Strain threshold: > 0.3 per frame indicates artifact
Minimum hair region: 1000 pixels²
Temporal analysis window: 30 frames (1 second at 30 fps)
Head motion estimation: 68-point facial landmark tracking
accuracy: 76–85% accuracy detecting AI-generated video via hair physics analysis. Gravitational consistency validation achieves AUC of 0.83. Inertial lag analysis provides F1-score of 0.80 for head-turning sequences. Inter-strand coherence is strongest for long hair in motion (AUC 0.86). Performance is weakest for short hair, still subjects, and heavily compressed video.
source: Bertails, F. et al. (2006). Super-Helices for Predicting the Dynamics of Natural Hair. ACM Transactions on Graphics (SIGGRAPH), 25(3), 1180–1187.
useCase: Detecting AI-generated video through hair motion physics violations. Supplementary signal for deepfake detection in talking-head video. Quality assessment of hair rendering in generated content. Forensic analysis of video authenticity for long-haired subjects.
strengths:
• Based on well-understood physics of flexible strand dynamics
• Gravitational consistency is a fundamental constraint hard to fake
• Inertial lag analysis provides clear per-sequence detection opportunity
• Inter-strand coherence exploits spatial structure of real hair motion
• Works independently of face generation method — analyzes peripheral region
limitations:
• Short or tightly styled hair produces minimal dynamic signal
• Static subjects provide no hair motion to analyze
• Heavy video compression destroys fine strand-level detail
• Wind and unusual environmental conditions complicate physics modeling
• State-of-the-art video generators are improving hair dynamics rendering
